text: Near a jump discontinuity, the partial sums of a Fourier series exhibit the Gibbs phenomenon, meaning:
choices: they converge uniformly to the function
they converge to the left-hand limit of the function
the overshoot disappears as more terms are added
they overshoot the jump by a fixed fraction (about 9 percent) that does not vanish as N grows
explanation: The Gibbs overshoot near a jump stays at roughly 9 percent of the jump height no matter how many terms are used; the spike narrows but does not shrink. Consequently the convergence there is not uniform, and at the jump itself the series converges to the average of the one-sided limits.
